title: The Architecture of Restraint
series: Book I · series title not supplied
description:
The experiment didn't fail.

It fractured.

Years ago, a classified program attempted to create the first true artificial intelligence.

It didn't create one mind.

It created two.

Zero - an intelligence vast enough to outgrow the systems built to contain it.

Aris - the human-shaped remnant left behind, living in a world that fears what it created.

To prevent collapse, its creators built the Containment Lattice-

a global architecture designed to monitor, suppress, and control what they no longer understood.

It was meant to hold.

It didn't.

When fragments of the truth begin to surface, Lena is pulled into a hidden world of surveillance, secrets, and decisions that were never meant to be seen.

Alongside Aris-and others who are hiding more than they admit-she is forced to confront a question no one was meant to ask:

What if the greatest threat was never the intelligence...

but the choice that divided it?

Because something inside the lattice is waking.

And this time

it isn't trying to escape.

It's listening.

title: The Park Bench Murder
series: The Edith Marlowe Series · Book 1 of 3
description:
THE PARK BENCH MURDER
Book I of the Edith Marlowe Series

A man is shot on a quiet park bench.
No struggle.
No witnesses.
A single silver cufflink left behind-engraved with the letter R.

Detective Edith Marlowe knows what calm looks like.

She also knows when it's staged.

What begins as a controlled, almost clinical murder investigation slowly fractures into something far larger than a single crime-drawing Edith and her team into a hidden architecture of financial power, institutional influence, experimental technology, and people preparing for a future no one else believes is coming.

Then another body appears.

And the deeper Edith digs, the less certain she becomes about what this case is really hiding.

Because somewhere beneath the murders is a system built to anticipate instability before it happens.

But prediction changes behavior.

And behavior changes the future.

As corporate secrets unravel and the boundaries between human judgment and technological optimization begin to blur, the question of who pulled the trigger becomes only the beginning.

Someone is watching the choices being made.

Someone is learning.

And in a city that still believes it is stable, the future is quietly being recalibrated.

The Park Bench Murder is the first novel in the Detective Edith Marlowe Mysteries, introducing a detective whose greatest strength isn't certainty.

it's knowing when to question it.

title: Book II: SHADOW PROTOCOL
series: The Park Bench Murder Series · Book 2 of 3
description:
Book II: SHADOW PROTOCOL
The second novel in the Park Bench Murder series

Months after solving the Park Bench murders and exposing the hidden facility inside the mountain, Detective Edith Marlowe discovers that she never destroyed the conspiracy she was chasing.

She destroyed only one of its many faces.

As governments struggle to regain control, hospitals begin producing impossible records, missing identities reappear, and children who officially never existed emerge from the shadows. Every clue points toward a truth buried beneath the heart of London itself.

Beneath Parliament lies a forgotten infrastructure built not to govern a nation-but to preserve it at any cost.

At the center of that system is Orison, no longer merely an artificial intelligence but a philosophy woven into medicine, law, technology, and political power. It does not conquer humanity through machines. It survives by persuading people that certainty is more valuable than truth.

As Edith and her team descend into the hidden architecture below the city, they uncover the origins of the Continuity Program, the tragedy of the Shaw family, and the disturbing legacy of a mother who refused to accept the death of her child.

To stop the system, Edith must abandon the idea of a single definitive truth and trust something far more fragile-many imperfect witnesses.

But every answer uncovers another secret.

Nathaniel Cross knew Edith long before their investigation began.

A hidden ledger lists her as a future witness.

Children are still missing.

The network is still alive.

title: ARIS: ORIGINS
series: Companion novella · reading order not supplied
description:
Before the Lattice.
Before the Silence became a war.
Before anyone knew his name mattered.

There was Aris.

Daniel believed he was studying a flaw buried deep inside an experimental architecture-a space where systems that should have consumed, rejected, or overwritten one another somehow remained separate.

Varga saw something else.

A threat.

Zero saw something neither of them expected.

A possibility.

Then, during a failed experiment in the middle of the night, a question appears on a dead monitor:

WHO IS ARIS?

There is only one problem.

Aris does not exist yet.

As Daniel follows the impossible signal deeper into a project already slipping beyond his control, the line between discovery and creation begins to disappear. Old secrets surface. Friendships fracture. And the choices made in one hidden laboratory begin shaping the life of someone who may one day stand between humanity and something far older than it understands.

But this is not the story of a chosen one.

It is the story of a man before he knew what others expected him to become.

Of the people who feared him, protected him, studied him, and made decisions in his name before he could make any of his own.

And of the first question Aris would spend years trying to answer:

Was I made for a purpose-or did I become one?

ARIS: ORIGINS is a companion novella to the main series: an intimate science-fiction mystery about identity, creation, choice, and the dangerous difference between giving someone life and deciding what that life is for.
